applicability_policy.local_derived: May mark network transport N/A only when no source acquisition occurs; execution, identity, retention, path, and resource boundaries still require explicit assessment.
applicability_policy.not_applicable: Requires scope, rationale, and evidence; cannot avoid an existing platform control.
applicability_policy.omission: Invalid; absence never implies no network, retention, replay, timeout, authorization, or identity binding.
applicability_policy.required_for_every_dimension: Every family records APPLICABLE or NOT_APPLICABLE for all 36 dimensions. Optional raw/replay features also explicitly say supported/provided or unsupported/not provided.

cross_phase_inheritance: Every family inherits L1 operability, L2 replay/retention/migration classification, L3 applicable source drift, and L4 security/resource controls.
deprecation_policy: Deprecation is explicit governance state, not deletion.
Historical retained artifacts remain readable under their declared version or fail closed explicitly.
A deprecated identity never silently points to new semantics.
Source deprecation never rewrites historical provenance.
Removal, migration, or compatibility break requires separate Owner authorization.

cardinality_rules.capability_to_executor: N:M across product; each resolved context selects exactly one trusted executor; blocked/contract-only contexts may select zero.
cardinality_rules.capability_to_typed_evidence_contract: N:M explicitly permitted; one contract may support multiple capabilities and one capability may compose multiple contracts.
cardinality_rules.mapping_rule: No mapping inferred from names or 1:1 assumptions; never collapse namespaces or add a second registry.
cardinality_rules.source_to_executor: N:M across product; actual bounded binding is explicit.
cardinality_rules.typed_evidence_to_source_contract: N:M explicitly permitted; multiple source contracts can normalize to one stable typed contract and one source may feed multiple projections.

namespace_policy.evidence_family_identity: Architecture/conformance concept established by explicit mappings across existing authorities.

namespaces.capability_id: Public request/data_need intent and parameters; Unified Request and canonical Capability Catalog.
namespaces.executor_id: Trusted implementation identity; current executor metadata and closed callable binding.
namespaces.routing_identity: Existing Request planning authority plus capability/market/target route and output binding; current routing matrix/resolver.
namespaces.source_authority_identity: Approved source identity and activation; existing source authority.
namespaces.source_contract_id: Provider/dataset/request-response acquisition semantics; existing source contract/authority.
namespaces.typed_evidence_contract_id: Normalized evidence semantics/version; existing typed schema and accepted family contract.

negative_invariants: No universal runtime family registry merely for extensibility.
No second Catalog/source/executor/identity authority, request protocol, or Result/Audit system.
No dynamic third-party execution, Python entry points, discovery, or hot loading.
No hidden acquisition or automatic source/capability activation.
No trading, order routing, or broker credentials.
registration_policy: Use existing authorities. Preserve intentional independent checks and synchronized views; no dynamic discovery or new family registry.
scope: Minimum declaration, ownership, registration, versioning, applicability, and conformance proof for a future evidence family. No family is added or activated.
version_transition_authority: T1-T12 and VER-01..VER-08 in the A1 run; each transition is conditional on its stated change.
